To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we used a novel method of analyzing RNA-seq data to identify genes that may be involved in the host response to NDV.

we identified novel candidate genes and gene networks associated with NDV challenge status, dpi post-infection, and genetic line that may be important in the host response to NDV infection and may be important for disease resistance.

the transcriptomic responses of Fayoumi and White Leghorn chicken lines to lentogenic ND virus challenge are differentially expressed, and that the response to challenge in the three tissues is more complex than previously understood.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new strategies for improving animal health, and the results from this study provide new insights into host response to NDV and may be applied to the development of new and improved disease control strategies.
the identification and characterization of host genetic factors that can improve the health of poultry.
the development of novel approaches to identify genes and networks involved in host resistance to NDV and to other pathogens in general, which can be used to improve animal health and production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study identified genes, networks, and pathways that were important for host response to a lentogenic NDV vaccine strain and may lead to a better understanding of the mechanisms that contribute to resistance to NDV and other diseases.
the combined transcriptomic data from three tissues, using a WGCNA approach, identified genes, pathways, and networks that were associated with genetic line, dpi, and challenge status.
WGCNA is a powerful and robust tool for analyzing complex biological systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combined transcriptome of three tissues from a resistant and susceptible line of chickens after lentogenic NDV vaccine challenge provides a more robust understanding of the host response to this pathogen than that obtained by studying each tissue individually.

the use of a novel bioinformatics method, WGCNA, in combination with RNA-seq, can provide a better understanding of the complex interactions between host and pathogen, leading to the identification of novel candidate genes for disease resistance.
by jointly analyzing the tissues, this study identifies genes and gene networks leading to a more comprehensive whole animal response to NDV than by individually analyzing the tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of WGCNA and RNA-seq can be a powerful tool for identifying genes associated with disease resistance and susceptibility.
the host response to NDV is a whole animal process and that the host response is tissue specific, but that there are also shared host responses to NDV.
the host response is complex and tissue-specific.
